title: OpenTelemetry Basics
description: Learn OpenTelemetry, the open-source standard for microservices observability.

data.text: OpenTelemetry (OTel) is an open-source observability framework that provides a single standard for traces, metrics, and logs. Google, Microsoft, and Amazon all contribute to OpenTelemetry, which is becoming the de facto standard for cloud-native observability.

OpenTelemetry provides APIs, SDKs, and tools to instrument, generate, collect, and export telemetry data. It replaces vendor-specific agents and SDKs with a single, vendor-neutral instrumentation layer.

data.title: Core Components
items: SDK: Implementation of the API with processing and exporting
Collector: Vendor-agnostic proxy for receiving, processing, and exporting telemetry
Protocol: OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) for data transmission
Auto-instrumentation: Zero-code instrumentation for popular frameworks

data.title: Vendor Neutral
data.text: OpenTelemetry decouples instrumentation from backends. You can send data to Jaeger, Zipkin, Datadog, New Relic, or any other backend without changing your instrumentation code.

items.question: Do I need a collector?
items.answer: No, but it is recommended. The collector provides batching, retries, and routing. You can export directly from the SDK for simple setups.

items.question: How does OpenTelemetry compare to OpenTracing and OpenCensus?
items.answer: OpenTelemetry merged OpenTracing and OpenCensus into a single project. It is the successor to both and is now the standard.

items.question: Does OpenTelemetry add overhead?
items.answer: Minimal. Auto-instrumentation is optimized for performance. Sampling (e.g., 1% of traces) reduces overhead further while maintaining visibility.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: OpenTelemetry is the open standard for observability
Provides vendor-neutral instrumentation for traces, metrics, and logs
Use OTLP for data transmission to any backend
data.takeaway: Adopt OpenTelemetry for unified observability across all your microservices.
